trials.notes: Used the correct structural processor, all called methods are documented, and the depth-bounded `next_token()` subtree walk matches the docs. It correctly used `is_string()` for `href` and read decoded text only from `#text` tokens. Minor nit: scanning all tokens for `A` is a little less direct than `next_tag( 'A' )`.

Correct processor and no undocumented APIs. `get_token_name() === 'A'` is documented and works, though `get_token_type() === '#tag'` plus `get_tag()` is the clearer opener-test pattern shown more often in the docs. Attribute and text edge semantics were handled well.

Correct processor and all methods are documented. The one-pass state machine follows the docs' advice for explicit token-walking state, but it manually reconstructs open-link state and close-depth behavior that the simpler documented bounded subtree walk already provides. The final LIFO flush is a near-miss pattern for repeated unclosed tracked elements, though it passed this task's cases.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed: all three trials passed 8/8 and produced no `_doing_it_wrong` records. The docs succeeded on the key points: `Which processor should I use?` and `Supported elements` steer structure/text tasks to `WP_HTML_Processor`; `Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree` shows the exact depth-bounded `next_token()` plus `#text` plus `get_modifiable_text()` pattern; `get_attribute()` documents `string|true|null`; `get_modifiable_text()` states decoded text semantics; and `next_token()`/`get_current_depth()` explain virtual closers and missing end tags. Near-misses were mostly around over-engineering: trial 3 built its own open-element stack, and trials 1/2 used nested token walks despite the repeated-regions warning, but the documented contracts were strong enough to keep the implementations valid.

doc_gaps.location: /tmp/html-api-docs-eval/round-76/html-processor.md — `Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree` / repeated-regions warning
doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn against nested `next_token()` loops for repeated regions, but the subtree recipe itself uses a bounded inner walk. This can leave readers unsure when consuming a whole subtree is safe versus when one stateful loop is required.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short distinction: bounded inner walks are appropriate when the caller intends to consume and skip the matched subtree; use one stateful loop when outer logic must observe every token, overlapping region, or boundary token.

doc_gaps.problem: The return type and example imply the boolean/missing/value distinction, but there is no explicit idiom for accepting only attributes written with a value.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note: use `is_string( $processor->get_attribute( $name ) )` to accept string-valued attributes, including `''`, and reject missing attributes and valueless boolean attributes.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain virtual closers and incomplete tokens, but the difference between an omitted normal end tag and a truly incomplete trailing syntax token could be easier to recognize.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact example showing an unclosed normal element at EOF still producing text and a virtual closing token, while `paused_at_incomplete_token()` remains separate from ordinary missing end-tag recovery.
